issues.legal_issue: Classifying tenants by net income for access to statutory rent protection is consistent with the constitutional guarantee of equality when the classification serves the protection of economically weaker tenants and the encouragement of building construction.
material_facts: A tenant sought protection under rent-control legislation, but the lower courts held that the tenant’s net income placed it outside the legislation’s protection.
The legislation applied its rent protection according to the tenant’s net income, including income earned inside or outside the state.
The challenge contended that the income distinction was arbitrary and unrelated to the legislation’s purpose.
The legislation aimed both to protect economically weaker tenants and to encourage construction of buildings.
issues.conclusion: The income-based classification is reasonable and does not violate Article 14 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 14, a classification is permissible when it rests on an intelligible differentia and that differentia has a rational relation to the statute’s object, as stated in Krishna Dalmia v. Shri Justice S.R. Tendolkar. An income-based classification can rationally serve the twin aims of protecting economically weaker tenants and encouraging construction. The Court approved J & K Bank Ltd. v. State of J & K, distinguished Rattan Arya v. State of Tamil Nadu and Motor General Traders v. State of Andhra Pradesh, and relied on Kerala Hotel & Restaurant Association v. State of Kerala. It also observed that legislative social and economic experimentation should not be displaced absent blatant disregard of constitutional provisions.

predicates.appeal_challenges_income_based_rent_prot: A party in an appeal challenges a legal classification that determines access to rent protection by reference to a tenant’s income.
predicates.rent_protection_targets_economically_wea: The rent-protection scheme is intended to protect tenants with less economic capacity from unreasonable eviction or unfair rent.
predicates.classification_encourages_building_const: The classification is designed in part to encourage the construction of buildings.
predicates.tenant_income_indicates_financial_capaci: The classification uses a tenant’s income as an indicator of the tenant’s financial capacity.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an income-based rent-protection classification and the stated predicates describe its purposes and basis, the classification satisfies equality.

issues.legal_issue: The concepts of income and net income are sufficiently clear to apply an income-based threshold for rent protection.
material_facts: The legislation excluded a tenancy from rent protection when the tenant’s income exceeded a specified threshold and explained that income meant net income.
The challenge argued that the legislation did not specify which deductions were allowed in calculating net income.
The Court treated income as a periodic monetary or other benefit, gain, profit, or revenue rather than capital, and net income as income after deducting expenses incurred to earn it.
issues.conclusion: The concepts of income and net income are not vague; net income is ordinarily understood as income less the expenses incurred to earn it.
issues.legal_principle: Income means money or another benefit periodically received and represents profit or revenue, not capital. Net income is income after deducting expenses incurred for the purpose of earning it, understood in ordinary common usage and not necessarily confined by fiscal enactments. The Court referred to Banarasi Das v. Jagdish Raj Kohli.

predicates.income_threshold_rent_protection_case: The case concerns rent protection whose availability depends on a tenant’s income.
predicates.income_is_periodic_gain_not_capital: The income used in the case consists of a periodically received gain, profit, revenue, or benefit rather than capital.
predicates.net_income_deducts_expenses_of_earning_i: The net amount is calculated by deducting expenses incurred to earn the income.

issues.definition: In an income-threshold rent-protection case, a standard based on periodic gain and net of expenses incurred to earn it is sufficiently clear.
